arxiv-2011-13900.title: Persuasion Produces the (Diamond) Paradox
arxiv-2011-13900.creator: Mark Whitmeyer
arxiv-2011-13900.description: Abstract This paper extends the sequential search model of Wolinsky 1986 by allowing firms to choose how much match value information to disclose to visiting consumers. This restores the Diamond paradox ( Diamond 1971 ): there exist no symmetric equilibria in which consumers engage in active search, so consumers obtain zero surplus and firms obtain monopoly profits.

arxiv-2204-06784.title: A crowdsourcing approach to video quality assessment
arxiv-2204-06784.creator: Babak Naderi, Ross Cutler
arxiv-2204-06784.description: Abstract The gold standard for measuring video quality is the subjective test, and the most prevalent is the ITU-T Rec. P.910, a lab-based subjective standard in use for the past two decades. However, in practice using ITU-T Rec. P.910 is slow, expensive, and requires a lab, which all create barriers to usage.

arxiv-2210-16553.title: Geometry of Diophantine exponents Thanks: This research has been financed by the Russian Science Foundation grant 22-21-00079, https://rscf.ru/project/22-21-00079/
arxiv-2210-16553.creator: Oleg N. German
arxiv-2210-16553.description: Abstract Diophantine exponents are ones of the simplest quantitative characteristics responsible for the approximation properties of linear subspaces of a Euclidean space. This survey is aimed at describing the current state of the area of Diophantine approximation which studies Diophantine exponents and relations they satisfy.

arxiv-2211-11621.title: Tilting refractive x-ray lenses for fine-tuning of their focal length Journal: oe Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2211-11621.creator: Rafael Celestre 1,*, Thomas Roth 1, Carsten Detlefs 1, Peng Qi 2, Marco Cammarata 1, Manuel Sanchez del Rio 1, Raymond Barrett 1
arxiv-2211-11621.description: Abstract In this work, we measure and model tilted x-ray refractive lenses to investigate their effects on an x-ray beam. The modelling is benchmarked against at-wavelength metrology obtained with x-ray speckle vector tracking experiments (XSVT) at the BM05 beamline at the ESRF-EBS light source, showing very good agreement.

arxiv-2212-10526.title: Open Domain Multi-document Summarization: A Comprehensive Study of Model Brittleness under Retrieval
arxiv-2212-10526.creator: John Giorgi, Luca Soldaini, Bo Wang, Gary Bader, Kyle Lo, Lucy Lu Wang, Arman Cohan
arxiv-2212-10526.description: Abstract Multi-document summarization (MDS) assumes a set of topic-related documents are provided as input. In practice, this document set is not always available; it would need to be retrieved given an information need, i.e. a question or topic statement, a setting we dub ‘‘open-domain’’ MDS.

arxiv-2302-08114.title: Energy decay for wave equations with a potential and a localized damping Thanks: Corresponding author: xiaoyanli@hust.edu.cn
arxiv-2302-08114.creator: Ryo Ikehata
arxiv-2302-08114.description: Abstract We consider the total energy decay together with L 2 L^{2} -bound of the solution itself of the Cauchy problem for wave equations with a localized damping and a short-range potential. We treat it in the one dimensional Euclidean space 𝐑 {\bf R} . We adopt a simple multiplier method to study them.

arxiv-2406-06205.title: Rooted trees with level structures, Ω \Omega -classes and double ramification cycles
arxiv-2406-06205.creator: Xavier Blot, Danilo Lewański, Sergey Shadrin
arxiv-2406-06205.description: Abstract . We prove a new system of relations in the tautological ring of the moduli space of curves involving stable rooted trees with level structure decorated by the top Chern class of the Hodge bundle and Ω \Omega -classes and double ramification structures.

arxiv-2407-08930.title: Resource-aware scheduling of multiple quantum circuits on a hardware device
arxiv-2407-08930.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by . Recent quantum technologies and quantum error-correcting codes emphasize the requirement for arranging interacting qubits in a nearest-neighbor (NN) configuration while mapping a quantum circuit onto a given hardware device, in order to avoid undesirable noise. It is equally important to minimize the wastage of qubits in a quantum hardware device with m m qubits while running circuits of n n qubits in total, with n < m n<m .

arxiv-2408-00748.title: Free boundary Hamiltonian stationary Lagrangian discs in ℂ 2 \mathbb{C}^{2}
arxiv-2408-00748.creator: Filippo Gaia
arxiv-2408-00748.description: Abstract . Let Ω ⊂ ℂ 2 \Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^{2} be a smooth domain. We establish conditions under which a weakly conformal, branched Ω \Omega -free boundary Hamiltonian stationary Lagrangian immersion u u of a disc in ℂ 2 \mathbb{C}^{2} is a Ω \Omega -free boundary minimal immersion.

arxiv-2503-03736.title: Opportunistic Routing in Wireless Communications via Learnable State-Augmented Policies
arxiv-2503-03736.creator: Sourajit Das, Kirtan Gopal Panda, Navid NaderiAlizadeh
arxiv-2503-03736.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sourajit Das, Kirtan Gopal Panda, Navid NaderiAlizadeh. This paper addresses the challenge of packet-based information routing in large-scale wireless communication networks. The problem is framed as a constrained statistical learning task, where each network node operates using only local information. Opportunistic routing exploits the broadcast nature of wireless communication to dynamically select optimal forwarding nodes, enabling the information to reach the destination through multiple relay nodes simultaneously.

arxiv-2507-00485.title: PNAct: Crafting Backdoor Attacks in Safe Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2507-00485.creator: Weiran Guo, Guanjun Liu, Ziyuan Zhou, Ling Wang
arxiv-2507-00485.description: Abstract Reinforcement Learning (RL) is widely used in tasks where agents interact with an environment to maximize rewards. Building on this foundation, Safe Reinforcement Learning (Safe RL) incorporates a cost metric alongside the reward metric, ensuring that agents adhere to safety constraints during decision-making.

arxiv-2512-09039.title: Microscopic Theory Revealing Dual Field-Induced Transitions in Spin- 1 2 \frac{1}{2} Screw-Chain Magnets
arxiv-2512-09039.creator: Mandev Bhullar, Philip Richard, Hae-Young Kee
arxiv-2512-09039.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mandev Bhullar, Philip Richard, Hae-Young Kee. We develop a microscopic theory for pseudospin- 1 2 \frac{1}{2} screw-chain compounds with spin-orbit coupling that goes beyond the phenomenological site-dependent g g -tensor description traditionally used for XXZ-like BaCo 2 V 2 O 8 and related materials.

It has been estimated that approximately 3.2 million deaths each year are attributable to insufficient levels of physical activity. We evaluat

pmc-10731154.title: Emerging space for non-polyethene-glycol bowel preparations in inflammatory bowel disease-related colonoscopy: Veering toward better adherence and palatability
pmc-10731154.creator: Raffaele Pellegrino, Antonietta Gerarda Gravina
pmc-10731154.description: Patients with inflammatory bowel diseases (IBDs) require repeated endoscopic evaluations over time by colonoscopy to weigh disease activity but also for different and additional indications (e.g., evaluation of postoperative recurrence, colorectal cancer surveillance). Colonoscopy, however, requires adequate bowel preparation to be of quality.

pmc-11335616.title: Identifying tinnitus in mice by tracking the motion of body markers in response to an acoustic startle
pmc-11335616.creator: Mark N. Wallace, Joel I. Berger, Adam Hockley, Christian J. Sumner, Michael A. Akeroyd, Alan R. Palmer, Peter A. McNaughton
pmc-11335616.description: Rodent models of tinnitus are commonly used to study its mechanisms and potential treatments. Tinnitus can be identified by changes in the gap-induced prepulse inhibition of the acoustic startle (GPIAS), most commonly by using pressure detectors to measure the whole-body startle (WBS). Unfortunately, the WBS habituates quickly, the measuring system can introduce mechanical oscillations and the response shows considerable variability.

pmc-11360085.title: Modulation of Growth and Mycotoxigenic Potential of Pineapple Fruitlet Core Rot Pathogens during In Vitro Interactions
pmc-11360085.creator: Manon Vignassa, Christian Soria, Noël Durand, Charlie Poss, Jean-Christophe Meile, Marc Chillet, Sabine Schorr-Galindo
pmc-11360085.description: Pineapple Fruitlet Core Rot (FCR) is a fungal disease characterized by a multi-pathogen pathosystem. Recently, Fusarium proliferatum, Fusarium oxysporum, and Talaromyces stollii joined the set of FCR pathogens until then exclusively attributed to Fusarium ananatum. The particularity of FCR relies on the presence of healthy and diseased fruitlets within the same infructescence.

pmc-11455383.title: 8080 Factors Affecting Survival of Lymph Node Positive Medullary Thyroid Cancer: A Population-Based Study From Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) Program
pmc-11455383.creator: Mohamed Mortagy, Aya Abdelhameed, Mohamed Tharwat Hegazy
pmc-11455383.description: Disclosure: M. Mortagy: None. A. Abdelhameed: None. M. Hegazy: None. Introduction: 50-70% of patients with MTC have positive lymph nodes. The Aim is to identify factors affecting survival of the lymph node positive MTC sub-population. Understanding these factors is important in treating these patients.

pmc-12432321.title: Metagenomic Insights Into Biopile Remediation of Petroleum-Contaminated Soil Using Chicken Droppings in Rivers State, Nigeria
pmc-12432321.creator: Emmanuel O Fenibo, Rosina Nkuna, Tonderayi Matambo
pmc-12432321.description: Petroleum hydrocarbon pollution is an escalating global issue, particularly in developing countries, where it has attracted significant attention from researchers focusing on bioremediation, monitoring and sustainability. This study utilised metagenomics to investigate the bacterial community’s response in polluted soil undergoing field-scale biopile treatment, with chicken droppings as a nutrient source.

pmc-13073600.title: Diels–Alder Adducts from Maytenus chiapensis
pmc-13073600.creator: Ulises G. Castillo, Morena L. Martínez, Marvin J. Núñez, Aday González-Bakker, José M. Padrón, Nathália Nocchi, Eduardo Hernández-Álvarez, Ignacio A. Jiménez, Isabel L. Bazzocchi
pmc-13073600.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Natural products from plants have played an important role in cancer and neurodegenerative diseases. In this context, the root bark of Maytenus chiapensis (Celastraceae) was investigated to examine its chemical constituents and potential biological activities. Chromatographic separation of the root bark extract yielded a new Diels–Alder adduct (morenine) formed by a triterpenophenolic moiety derived from tingenone and a bicyclic guaiane-type sesquiterpene linked through a 1,4-dioxane bridge.

pmc-13508564.title: Consanguinity-Associated Genetic Disorders in Saudi Arabia: A Hypothesis on the Future Role of CRISPR-Based Gene Editing
pmc-13508564.creator: Dana Aldughim

pmc-13538695.title: Supportive care needs among patients with breast and cervical cancer at a tertiary cancer treatment center in ethiopia: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13538695.creator: Bedilu Deribe Derese, Eva Johanna Kantelhardt, Thomas Frese, Betty Ferrell, Muluken Gizaw, Sefonias Getachew, Abigiya Wondimagegnehu, Adamu Addissie, Eric Sven Kroeber, Lesley Taylor, Susanne Unverzagt
pmc-13538695.description: The rising incidence of cancer diagnoses alongside improving survival rates in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) has substantially increased the demand for comprehensive supportive care. This study aimed to assess the supportive care needs of patients diagnosed with breast or cervical cancer at Hawassa University Comprehensive Specialized Hospital Cancer Treatment Center, Ethiopia.

uslaw-usc-t16-s3163.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t16-s3163.description: United States Code, Title 16 (Conservation); Chapter 51 (Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation); Subchapter IV (Transportation And Utility Systems In And Across, And Access Into, Conservation System Units). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Except as specifically provided for in this subchapter, applicable law shall apply with respect to the authorization and administration of transportation or utility systems.
